newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-COLLYMORE SAYS HE'S STAYING AT ANFIELD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLLYMORE SAYS HE'S STAYING AT ANFIELD.

text.p: Stan Collymore marked his return to the Liverpool first side with a goal after just 40 seconds on Saturday and then said he was not about to quit Anfield.

Collymore, who signed for Liverpool for a club record 8.5 million pounds ($14.3 million) from Nottingham Forest in June 1995, has been at the centre of transfer speculation this week after being banished to the substitutes' bench for eight consecutive games before Saturday's 1-1 home draw with Wimbledon.

English newspapers claimed he was set to move to Aston Villa, just down the road from his Midlands home town of Cannock in Staffordshire, which he has consisently refused to abandon for the bright lights of Merseyside.
But after helping the 18 times English champions to a point with an opportunistic goal at the start of Saturday's match, the 25-year-old said he was happy to stay put at Liverpool.
"There's been a lot of things said in the newspapers but I'm not thinking of leaving Liverpool," he told BBC radio.

"I don't see the need to leave my home in the Midlands," he said when asked why he did not live in Liverpool. "I've got a great set up there with lots of good friends...but I've no intention of leaving Anfield. I'm very happy here."

The powerful Collymore was an instant hit with Liverpool fans last season, scoring on his debut and going on to notch a further 18 goals as his side reached the F.A. Cup final and pushed hard for the league title.

But this year he has been overshadowed by England striker Robbie Fowler and new signing Patrik Berger of the Czech Republic, who has scored six goals in 11 appearances, of which only five have been over a full 90 minutes.
Only because Steve McManaman limped out of Wednesday night's Merseyside derby with Everton with a serious hamstring injury did Collymore get the chance to start on Saturday.
And a chance was all he needed.
With less than a minute on the clock Collymore pounced on a mistake by Wimbledon defender Dean Blackwell and guided a shot past Neil Sullivan into the net for his fourth goal of the season.
Whether it will be enough to keep "Stan the Man" in the first team on a long-term basis remains to be seen.
Collymore slipped through the scouting nets of several of England's major clubs and started his career at amateur club Stafford Rangers before moving on to Crystal Palace, Southend and Forest.
Once McManaman is back in the side, Liverpool's costliest player could find himself back on the bench again, and speculation over his next move is sure to resurface.
